recaps.title: Thirty-six goals, two six-point nights and one clean game
text: Arnie Jordan here, coming to you from row three at Jordan Arena, with the Rinkside Report, the only hockey podcast with two loyal listeners. Three, if my neighbour remembers. It was Sunday, October fourth. I had a coffee in one hand and a pencil in the other, and I needed both, because we had three games and thirty-six goals. Thirty-six. I ran out of page.

Game one was the Keg Canucks against Dawson's Oilers, and the Oilers put ten on the board in a ten to five win. From where I sat, Ron McPherson was everywhere, with two goals and four assists for six points. That's not a stat line, that's a phone number. Darren Craig had a goal and four helpers, and Mike Foran scored a pair. I will say there was one pass in that game that missed everybody on the ice, and I believe it is still on its way to Vineland. I didn't catch who threw it, and I'm not asking.

But give the Canucks their due. Down seven to two, they could have packed it in. Instead, Daryl Strong and Wes Short scored forty-five seconds apart to close out the second period, both set up by Waylon Tweedy and Kurt Peters, and Paul Koke had two of his own. I barely had the first one written down before the second one went in. The Oilers also took three trips to the penalty box and still won by five, so I'll keep my opinions to myself, at least this week.

Game two. I had just sat back down with a fresh coffee. The ColdBreak Leafs came out flying, with goals from Kevin Pierce, Larry Penney and Adam Steele, and they led three to one after the first period. I wrote the word upset in my notebook. I have since crossed it out, because the Regatta Nordiques scored eight in a row. Josh Moore had the hat trick and three assists, so that's six points for him as well. Doug Lawrence scored twelve seconds into the third, Moore scored again less than a minute later, and that was the hockey game.

Nine to three for the Nordiques, with two goals each for Lawrence and Nick Langlois, and four points for Adam Regular. And a tip of the cap to Kevin Rolston, who came into the Nordiques net halfway through and did not let in a single goal. He made it look so easy that I started wondering if I could do it. I could not. I get winded on the stairs up to row three.

Game three was the late one, the Culp Habs against the Timbit Senators, and the first period was a track meet. Drew Hering scored forty seconds in, before I had even sharpened my pencil, and then he got another. Matt Dixon added a third, and Kevin Paul set up all three of them. But every time the Habs scored, the Senators answered, with Blaine Davies, then Tyler Williams, then Davies again. It was tied at three after one.

After that, the Senators shut the door. Simon Murphy scored with fifty seconds left in the second and again in the third, and Rob Holt added one for insurance, for a six to three final. Davies and Murphy each had two goals and two assists, Dave Sheridan had three helpers, and Tim Shannon came in cold and stopped everything he saw. Somewhere in there, a shot went so wide that it rattled the glass right in front of me. I spilled half my coffee, and I would like the league to know that I am keeping the receipt.

And listen to this. There was not one penalty in that game. Sixty minutes of oldtimers hockey, and nobody went to the box. I keep a whole column in my notebook for penalties, and it is still empty. I didn't think it could be done.

So that's your week: thirty-six goals, two six point nights, and one game as clean as a whistle. If I got your name wrong, or gave your goal to the fella beside you, take it up with the refs, the timekeeper, and how fast you people move out there. All the details are on the league website. Tape your sticks, and give me a wave if you see me in row three on Sunday. This has been Arnie Jordan with the Rinkside Report.
